clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau's friend Lily lived in a castle in Malibu filled with family treasures, some centuries old, worth an estimated $400 million. None of it was insured - they were considered priceless.

Then a fire burned it all to the ground.

When Kevin called to tell her how sorry he was, she stopped him: "I was tired of cleaning that house. Time to move on, Kevin."

Not a performance. Not even a pause to think about it.

The idea he leads with: wanting what you don't have is the root of suffering. Lily just happened to live it.

#kevintrudeau #mindset #nonattachment #resilience #wealthmindset #personalgrowth

Kevin Trudeau met a 92-year-old lawyer still working at the Empire State Building - he started the day it opened. His wife had died years earlier: she was hit by a bus while they held hands on a New York sidewalk, mid-conversation about how much they loved each other.

Kevin asked how he dealt with it. "I cried every day for a week," he said. Then, six days in, he decided he'd grieved enough and went back to living.

That man, Kevin says, never got cancer and never took a drug in his life. He never held on to anything.

#kevintrudeau #mindset #grief #resilience #personalgrowth #letitgo

clips.end_words: Let it go. Let it go
clips.caption:
Go back far enough in history, Kevin Trudeau says, and every culture had a grieving period. In some, it was 30 days: women wore black, gathered, and wailed out loud, on purpose, every day, then took the black off and returned to their lives.

They were letting the energy out instead of burying it, he says, so it didn't turn into cancer later.

Most people today hold on to stuff for years - a bankruptcy, a lost job, a lover who left. It's a picture of a tiger, not an actual tiger. There's nothing left to be afraid of.

Let it go.

#kevintrudeau #mindset #grief #release #personalgrowth #letitgo
